title: A command interpreter with match
description:
Parse commands for a small game with structural pattern matching.

```
> go north
You walk north.
> take lamp
You take the lamp.
> take
Take what?
> inventory
You carry: lamp
> drop sword
You do not have a sword.
> quit
```

starter.main.py:
inventory = []
while True:
    words = input("> ").lower().split()
    match words:
        case ["quit"]:
            break
        # TODO: the other cases
        case _:
            print("I do not understand.")

hints: `case ["go", ("north" | "south" | "east" | "west") as direction]:` matches only the four directions (lesson 7.04).
Put `["take"]` before or after `["take", item]`: a two-item pattern never matches a one-item list, so the order does not matter there.
requirements: Split the line into words and `match` on the list: `["go", direction]`, `["take", item]`, `["take"]`, `["drop", item]`, `["inventory"]`, `["quit"]`.
Only `north`, `south`, `east` and `west` are directions (use a guard or an or-pattern).
Anything else prints `I do not understand.`
stretch: Accept `take the lamp` by matching `["take", "the", item]` too, and `go` with a first letter (`n`, `s`).
